summary: In major defense and commercial launch developments, SpaceX has won $1.6 billion in U.S. Space Force contracts to launch sensing and targeting satellite networks, as the federal government considers a proposed rule that would exempt commercial launch and spacecraft reentry licensing from environmental regulations. Expanding military space infrastructure, the Space Force awarded All Points $250 million to expand satellite processing at Vandenberg Space Force Base and announced plans to execute 18 communications and targeting missions by the end of 2027. In the commercial sector, K2 Space raised $500 million to expand its defense and commercial satellite operations, while defense contractor L3Harris postponed a planned initial public offering for its missile unit until mid-2027. On the civil space and planetary science front, NASA officially assigned astronaut Deniz Burnham to her first mission to the International Space Station, researchers identified the solar system's first three-headed asteroid accompanied by a moon, and NASA's Curiosity rover discovered honeycomb-like rock textures on Mars. Looking ahead, space observers should watch for the planned late August launch of NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.
